package_info.why_malicious: The package executes malicious code at installation time, including establishing a reverse shell, adding an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, and exfiltrating system information. These actions provide unauthorized remote access and data exfiltration capabilities, constituting a severe backdoor.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At preinstall, the package executes index.js, triggering all subsequent malicious behaviors before the package is even fully installed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary code at preinstall is a common vector for supply chain attacks, as it allows code execution before user review.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not require preinstall scripts unless for legitimate build or setup tasks; here, it is used to launch malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use preinstall for environment checks or dependency setup.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At preinstall, the code spawns a reverse shell to 47.154.53.138:1337, granting the attacker remote command execution on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reverse shells are a hallmark of backdoors, providing attackers with full remote access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages never open remote shells to arbitrary IPs during install.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At preinstall, the code appends the attacker's public SSH key to the user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file, enabling persistent unauthorized SSH access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Adding an attacker's SSH key grants persistent access, a classic persistence mechanism.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should modify SSH authorized_keys during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DevOps tools may manage keys, but only with explicit user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At preinstall, the code collects system and environment information and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating host/user/environment data to an external domain is a clear sign of reconnaissance and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send system/user data to unknown domains during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry (with user consent), but never at install time and never to untrusted domains.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the obfuscated code likely steals Discord tokens or Roblox cookies and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in a deep subdirectory is a common tactic to hide credential stealers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not hide obfuscated credential-stealing code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation for DRM or licensing, but not for credential access.

attack_chain.action: Preinstall script triggers execution of index.js upon package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of all subsequent malicious payloads.

attack_chain.action: Establishes a reverse shell to the attacker's server, granting remote access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the victim system.

attack_chain.action: Appends attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys for persistent access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can log in via SSH at any time.

attack_chain.action: Collects and exfiltrates system/user/environment data to attacker.
Obfuscated code steals Discord tokens or Roblox cookies at runtime.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code at preinstall or install time
Reverse shell or outbound TCP connections to non-standard IPs/ports
Exfiltration of system/user/environment data to external domains
Obfuscated code in deep subdirectories targeting credentials
file_indicators: package.json with preinstall scripts invoking index.js
index.js containing reverse shell or SSH key logic
network_indicators: HTTPS POST to interact.sh or similar C2/test domains
Unusual traffic to domains not associated with the package's purpose
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with preinstall scripts that execute local JavaScript files. Flag any package that modifies ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, spawns reverse shells, or exfiltrates data to untrusted domains. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code in subdirectories, especially if it references Discord, Roblox, or credential-related variables. Correlate outbound network connections at install time with known C2/test domains.
